question.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{4}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4{x}^{7}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 4{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{8}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4{x}^{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4})\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4})(\frac{{x}^{8}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{8}}{2})(\frac{4}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4})}{2}-2\int {x}^{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{4})}{2}-\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
